newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac not seen naming any candidate for premier.
newsitem.headline: Chirac not seen naming any candidate for premier.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac is not expected to spell out any preference for France's next prime minister before Sunday's second round of a parliamentary election, an official source said on Monday.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said earlier he would step down even if the centre-right coalition, which he has led for the last two years, reversed a combined left lead in the first round of voting.

Juppe himself had recognised before the first round vote that his personality was "a bit dry" to bring out the voters and he took most of the blame for unpopular austerity measures to prepare France for a single European currency.

Among politicians tipped to succeed Juppe are National Assembly president Philippe Seguin, a populist Eurosceptic, and ex-prime minster Edouard Balladur, who challenged Chirac for the presidency in 1995.
"There is no preferred candidate," the source said.
Chirac is expected to intervene in the election with an address to the nation, possibly as early as Tuesday night.
